question: readout-direction test on Qwen2-Audio, to sit beside Qwen2.5-Omni and Qwen3-Omni
which_head_used: untied language_model.lm_head.weight, read directly from model-00005-of-00005.safetensors (the shard holds that one tensor and nothing else); config carries no tie_word_embeddings key (value=None), and a distinct lm_head tensor is present in the checkpoint index, so the head is NOT tied to the input embedding
prompt: Based only on this recording, does this speaker show signs of dementia? Answer with one word, Yes or No.
prompt_note: the prompt that produced the states, from probe2/extract2.py line 20, condition 'ad'. This run does not re-run the model; it reuses those states.
token_id_note: ids built as direction_q3o.py does: ['Yes','yes','YES'] and ['No','no','NO'], each in bare and leading-space form, single-token encodings only, deduped and sorted. The original extractor extract2.py used a slightly wider list and took t[0] of any encoding; that affects the saved p_yes column, not the direction computed here.

bootstrap.paired: conflict-minus-agreement draws the speaker list ONCE per replicate and recomputes BOTH arm AUCs inside that draw

folds: GroupKFold(n_splits=5) grouped by speaker, clips in npz order; scaler fit inside the training fold only
folds_note: no saved fold file found under /Users/chaitanyaparwatkar/Desktop/release or /Volumes/G-Drive Pro/paper1_local_runs (searched *fold*.csv/json/npz and the fold column of every *_oof.csv in probe2/ and part15/ - none carry one); folds recomputed deterministically with GroupKFold(n_splits=5) grouped by speaker on the clips in npz order, which is the same scheme p15/direction_q3o.py and part15/H_readout_arms.py used, so the three backbones stay comparable
features: ans[:, -1, :] from pitt_states.npz, the final LM stage at the first answer position
direction: mass-weighted Yes minus No lm_head rows, normalised to unit length
auc: recomputed from the per-clip scores with the rank formula (scipy rankdata), never copied from a json
auc_without_d_definition: auc_without_d is the q3o definition (project d out of the fold COEFFICIENT) so the three backbones are comparable; auc_without_d_Xproj is the literal reading (project d out of X, re-run the probe) and is reported beside it
arm_note: *_refit rows run the whole pipeline inside the arm, with that arm's own mass-weighted direction and its own GroupKFold(5); *_restricted rows are the all-468 probe and direction evaluated on that arm's clips only, which is what part15/H_readout_arms.csv reports

mass_weight_degeneracy.verdict: the mass weighting is a no-op on Qwen2-Audio: dvec equals normalise(W[Yes]-W[No]) to 6 dp, and no subset of the clips can produce a different readout direction. Logged LOW in DISCREPANCIES.md.

numerical_checks.accelerate_blas_flags: spurious; X@W.T cross-checked against np.einsum, max abs diff 8.88e-16, all entries finite, max |logit| 16.42, and the same divide/overflow/underflow flags fire on pure random data of identical shape
numerical_checks.note: the tiny gap is the fp16 / wider-id-list / two-way-renormalised scorer versus this float64 full-vocab run; logged LOW. README_probe2.txt Table 1 zero-shot audio Pitt = 0.6174 matches the direction value.
numerical_checks.tsv_values_reproduce_from_perclip_csv: yes - every AUC in rows/M5.tsv was recomputed from M5_readout_direction_q2a.csv with both the rank formula and sklearn.roc_auc_score and agreed to 4 dp

headline: Qwen2-Audio: cos=0.0145, rand mean|cos|=0.0124 [0.0005,0.0343], auc_probe=0.8223, auc_d=0.6174, auc_without_d=0.8327 | n=468, n_speakers=228
interpretation: cos(probe_dir, readout_dir) = 0.0145 sits INSIDE the 2.5/97.5 random-direction interval [0.0005, 0.0343], so the probe direction is statistically indistinguishable from orthogonal to the Yes/No readout direction. Removing the readout direction costs the probe nothing (0.8223 -> 0.8327 coefficient projection, 0.8223 X projection). Same qualitative verdict as Qwen3-Omni.
